transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess what brings me in is my body’s been feeling kind of out of my control lately. At first I was just pacing around the apartment all night, making all these supper-club notes, and I thought maybe I was just being productive. But lately it’s the opposite—I’m so slowed down that my sister says it takes me forever just to get my shoes on. I don’t know if that makes sense.
Have you ever had a period of time when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or extremely irritable, where people around you noticed a change in your behavior?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but after I got fired I did feel kind of… strangely unstoppable? Like excited, like I had all these ideas and I was sure they were going to work.

And people did notice, I think. If anyone questioned what I was doing or told me to slow down, I’d get really upset—probably more than I should have. I’d snap at them, like they were trying to mess up my whole life. That’s not great, I know.

After that period of feeling unusually excited and full of ideas, did you experience a time when you felt down most of the day, lost interest in things you usually enjoy, or had trouble sleeping or eating?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to be dramatic about it, but things just got really flat after that. Like the stuff that usually keeps me kind of steady—cooking, taking pictures of food, listening to music, playing pickup soccer, even volunteering—it all just feels… muted, I guess.

I know I used to care about those things. I remember caring. But right now I can’t really make myself feel it, if that makes sense.
How long did you feel that way—like you were unstoppable and full of ideas?

It was… longer than I want to admit, honestly. Maybe around four months? It kind of started after I got fired from the restaurant, and I kept thinking it was just me trying to bounce back or stay motivated. But looking back, yeah… about four months. Does that sound like what you’re asking?
After that period of feeling really high and full of ideas, did you experience a time when you felt down most of the day, almost every day, and lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but after that it was like everything just went kind of flat.

The stuff that usually keeps me steady—cooking, taking food photos, music, pickup soccer, even volunteering—I know I used to care about all of it. I remember liking it. But lately I just can’t really make myself feel interested in any of it, if that makes sense.
How long did you feel that way—like things were flat and you couldn’t feel interested in the things you usually enjoy?

Um… it’s been a while. I’d say maybe about three months now that it’s felt like that — just heavy and slowed down. I kept thinking it would pass or I’d snap out of it, so I wasn’t really counting at first, but… yeah, around three months.

During the time you felt unusually excited and full of ideas, did you get so restless or hyperactive that you couldn’t sit still, or did you end up doing things that were unusually risky or out of character for you—like spending sprees, impulsive travel, or other actions that later seemed unwise?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say I was trying to be reckless exactly. It felt productive at the time, like I was just really motivated.

But I did have this nonstop energy for a while. Like I couldn’t sit through a meal, or even a soccer game, without jumping up to make calls, sketch out menu ideas, or start reorganizing the kitchen. It probably looked kind of intense from the outside. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Can you describe what your mood was like during that time when you felt so full of ideas and energy? Was it consistently elevated or irritable, and did it feel different from how you usually feel?

Yeah… it definitely felt different from my normal self. At first I honestly thought it was a good thing, like after getting fired I suddenly felt weirdly… unstoppable, I guess. Excited, like I had all these plans and maybe everything was going to work out better.

But I should probably say—without making it sound worse than it was—I wasn’t just happy. If someone questioned me or told me to slow down, I’d get really upset. Like, blow up at them, like they were trying to ruin my life or block me. I’m not proud of that. It just felt so intense at the time.

During that time when you felt so full of energy and ideas, did your behavior become so extreme that it caused serious problems in your life—like trouble with the law, financial crises, relationship breakdowns, or did you ever feel so out of control that someone thought you needed to be hospitalized?

I mean… I don’t think it was, like, criminal or anything. But yeah, it got pretty bad in practical terms.

I couldn’t really keep my work plans straight, and rent stuff got messed up, and I kept saying I’d handle family commitments but then I just… didn’t follow through. Or I’d start ten different things and none of the basic stuff got done.

My sister eventually took me to a crisis clinic, which is embarrassing to say. She said I wasn’t able to get normal responsibilities organized on my own, and… I guess she wasn’t wrong. Does that count as serious enough?
Have you had more than one period in your life when you felt unusually energetic, overly confident, or irritable to the point that it affected your behavior?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I’ve had times where I was more keyed up or more irritable than usual, but I don’t know if I’d call them the same as this.

This recent stretch is the one that really stands out to me as affecting how I acted. The other times… I don’t know, maybe I just thought of them as stress or being motivated. I don’t want to overstate it. Does that make sense?

Have you ever had another separate period in your life, different from the recent one you described, where you felt unusually energetic, overly confident, or irritable enough that it changed how you behaved?

I… I don’t think I can clearly point to another separate time like that, no.

I’ve had moments where I was more energetic or kind of overly confident, or where people said I was being intense, but I don’t know if it really changed my behavior in the same way. I don’t want to say yes if I’m just stretching it, you know?

The recent one is the only one I’m sure about.

Can you think of any other time in your life — even if it wasn’t as intense as this recent episode — where you felt unusually energetic, unusually confident, or unusually irritable for several days or more, and people around you noticed a change in how you were acting?

I guess… there was one time after I got fired where I felt weirdly, I don’t know, energized? Like I should’ve been scared or embarrassed, but instead I felt kind of unstoppable, like maybe it was actually a good thing and I had all these plans.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but people did notice. If someone questioned me or told me to slow down, I’d get really upset — like, way more than made sense. I’d feel like they were trying to ruin everything for me, and I’d kind of blow up.

So… yeah, I guess that probably counts?
Can you recall if there was a time when you had a noticeably elevated or irritable mood that lasted for at least four days, even if it wasn’t as extreme as the recent episode?

Yeah… I think that time after I got fired probably lasted at least several days. I was weirdly excited and felt kind of unstoppable, like I had all these ideas and plans and it was going to turn out great.

But I also got really touchy. If anyone questioned me or told me to slow down, I’d blow up at them, like they were trying to ruin my life or something. I’m not proud of that. I guess I was trying to frame it as motivation at the time, but looking back, it was noticeable.
